Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public. 




Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan 
"The Right to Information, The Right to Live"

IS : 5227 - 1969 




Indian Standard 
SPECIFICATION FOR FLASKS, DENTAL 



( Reaffirmed 1998) 



I. Scope — Dimensions and requirements of dental flasks for lower and upper dentures. 

1. Material— Aluminium alloy, Designation A-6M of IS: 6 1 7- 1 959* or brass, Grade 3 of IS: 292- 1 96 If. 

3. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. I, 2 and 3. 

4. Workmanship and Fmish — The castings of the flasks shall be clean and free from surface and casting 
flaws. The finished castings shall have a reasonably good finish and shall require no further machining 
except at the mating lugs. All sharp edges shall be rounded off. The two halves of the flask shall engage 
without any jerk and shall not leave any gap at the mating -edge when observed against light. 

5. Marking --The flasks shall be marked with the manufacturer's name, initials or recognized trade-mark, 
and country of manufacture. 

5.1 ISI Certification Morking — Details available from Indian Standards Institution. 

6. Packing-Each flask shall be suitably packed in polyethylene bag and then In card-board cartons. 
If required the flask may also be packed as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 




SHALLOW PART DEEP PART 

Ail dimensions in miiiimetres. 
FIG. I FLASK, DENTAL, FOR LOWER DENTURES
